offences.quote: Where a student has made unauthorised use of generative artificial intelligence within their assessment and has attempted to gain an unfair advantage by passing this work off as their own.

Students who fail to follow the instructions in the assignment brief and attempt to gain an unfair advantage by passing off work produced by generative artificial intelligence as their own may be investigated for academic misconduct in line with this policy.
The latter includes ‘hallucinated’ references, for example in instances where they have been generated by artificial intelligence.
Collusion is the undisclosed collaboration of two or more people on an assignment or task, which is supposed to be completed individually.
Self-plagiarism is submission by the student of work or large elements of work that has been submitted previously for academic credit, whether at this institution or another.

Examples of exam misconduct can include: copying from another candidate in an examination, bringing unsanctioned materials or devices into the examination room or gaining access to unauthorised materials prior to an examination.
Contract cheating happens when a third party completes work for a student who then submits it to an education provider as their own.

liability.quote: The student is in the first 12 months (or part-time equivalent) of their period of registered study, and can evidence that there is a valid reason that they may be less familiar than others with how to ensure academic integrity.
In some cases where a student has breached exam regulations, but there is no evidence they have cheated, some discretion may be applied regarding the application of the penalty.

detection.quote: Software such as Turnitin, or other packages to identify academic similarity reports, are indicative tools.
A high or low similarity score does not automatically result in either action or inaction.
Academic judgement will be required to determine whether collusion has taken place and by which parties.

process.quote: All suspected academic misconduct must be reported to Assessment Management as soon as suspected and it will be investigated in all cases.
All suspected academic misconduct must be reported to Assessment Management as soon as suspected and it will be investigated in all cases.
Where a potential case of academic misconduct has been identified, the student will be invited to attend an Academic Misconduct Investigation meeting.
The student will be given the opportunity to present their case and to provide any supporting evidence or information they wish to submit
If the student does not attend, and does not attempt to make alternative arrangements, the meeting can take place in the student’s absence.
The student may bring a representative to the meeting, normally an advisor from the Student Union Advice Centre.
A student who is in receipt of a penalty decision from a minor, major, or severe case has the right to appeal against the decision.
The appeal should be made within 10 working days of the date on which the decision outcome is sent.
The required standard of proof at any stage of the investigation is that the University is satisfied that, on the basis of the evidence available, that academic misconduct is likely to have occurred.
A record of the penalties applied in relation to academic misconduct will be retained in accordance with the University’s Records Retention and Disposal Schedule.

outcomes.quote: Minor cases will be dealt with in a supportive, developmental way.
Written warning and mark of 0 for the assessment being undertaken
Written warning and mark of 0 for the assessment being undertaken
Coursework: assignment re-marked without the identified elements being included for assessment.
Student deemed to have failed the course
Thesis is given an outcome of ‘resubmission’
If the student is required to be reassessed, any reassessment mark will be capped at the appropriate pass mark for that level.
In circumstances where the University becomes aware of an allegation of academic misconduct against a student after they have been granted an award, retrospective action can be taken.
When considering the level of penalty, the team will determine whether the student has had a prior record of academic misconduct (including minor cases, as above) and check on their level of study.
The severity of the offence, and consequently the penalty, will depend on the student’s academic level, whether it is a first or subsequent offence, and the level of use.
If a student on a PSRB course is found to have committed academic misconduct, they may be referred by their academic department for further consideration under the Fitness to Practise procedure.

definitions.quote: Academic misconduct occurs when a student does not follow good academic practice in an assessment, gaining unfair advantage and undermining academic standards.
Collusion is the undisclosed collaboration of two or more people on an assignment or task, which is supposed to be completed individually.
